content.text: Judging the item on its own demands, it is a two-part FRQ-style write-code task. Part (a) is a ceiling division using integer arithmetic, (minutes + 59) / 60, or an if/else that handles the remainder. It needs one integer-division subtlety and one boundary check at exactly 120 minutes and at 0. Part (b) calls hoursCharged and then uses nested or sequential conditionals for the tier structure: up to 2 hours at $4, additional hours at $3, and a $20 cap. This takes about three reasoning steps. The cap is only reached at 2 + 4*... = 8 + 3k > 20, which needs k >= 5, so 7 hours or more. The computation is tiny and the reading load is modest. The item uses legitimate difficulty levers (integer-division subtlety, boundary plausibility) and none of the banned sources, so it is a fair full-mock item. Writing code is expected of this skill (2.A), and the context is not extraneous.
